result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers sort commands into deterministic tiers and design strong prompts that show the exact target and whether the action can be undone. A goes further on scoped standing rules with caps, dry-run trials and expiring approvals. It also has a digest of auto-run actions with an Undo on each item, and it labels its numbers as starting values to test. B's server-side guardrails (RBAC and admission policies) are strong, but it lacks scoped grants and any way to reverse auto-run actions, and it states expected figures like '80%+ in Tier 0 and 1' without basis. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers sort actions into well-built tiers, use a deterministic classifier that fails closed, and give clear prompts for destructive actions. B does better on scoped standing rules with namespace and environment limits and caps, and on a digest of auto-run actions with an Undo on each item. It also says its numbers are starting values, not findings. A has no per-task or per-namespace grants beyond short approval expiry, and its audit log offers weekly review but no clear way to reverse an auto-run action.
